Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And
Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KRISHNA S.DIXIT  AND  THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL) This appeal is filed by the injured claimant seeking higher compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 22.08.2015 passed in M.V.C. No.33/2014 by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge, Belagavi (for short,
' the Trial Court)

. 
2. Brief facts of the case leading to filing of this appeal are that,
(a) The appellant/claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
stating on 25.08.2013, he was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-22/EK-7360 from Kakatives towards Kangrali B.K., near Channamma NC:
2024:KHC-D:11682-DB circle, and at that time, the driver of the goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-25/C-0441 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the motorcycle due to which he sustained grievous injury to his head.

It was stated that immediately after the accident,
he was shifted to KLE Hospital and was treated as an inpatient till 05.09.2013.

It was further stated that he was working as an Accountant in Chindak Distributors and getting monthly salary of Rs.15,000/- and due to the accidental injuries, he suffered disability and was unable to carryout any work.
Hence, he sought compensation for the injuries suffered by him.
(b) Notices were issued to owners and insurers of the motorcycle and goods vehicle.
Respondent No.1- owner of the goods vehicle though served with the notice, remained absent and was placed ex parte.
Other respondents entered appearance before the Trial Court and opposed the claim petition by NC: 2024:KHC-D:11682-DB denying the occurrence of accident and negligence of the goods vehicle.
They also denied the income and avocation of the appellant/claimant and also the injuries suffered by him.
Hence, they sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
(c) The Trial Court recorded the evidence of the parties.
The father of the claimant was examined as P.W.1 and Dr.Chandrashekar T.R., was examined as P.W.2.
The claimant got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.
Respondents did not adduce any oral evidence, but, with consent, marked insurance policies issued in respect of motorcycle and goods vehicle as Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.

The Trial Court, on consideration of the material on record, held that the rider of the motorcycle i.e., the Gangadhar vs Ashok S/O Shetteppa Haddali on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45970353/
3 claimant was negligent to an extent of 20% and the driver of the goods vehicle was negligent to an extent of 80%.

sentences.text: With regard to the quantum of compensation, the Trial Court considering the evidence on record, NC: 2024:KHC-D:11682-DB awarded a total compensation of 8,98,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
3. Sri. K.Anandkumar, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant, submits that the Trial Court committed a grave error in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.6,000/- per month.

He also submits that the Trial Court further committed a grave error in assessing the disability at 60% since the evidence of P.W.1 clearly indicates that the appellant/claimant is unable to carryout any activities and hence, the disability requires to be assessed at 100%.
He further submits that the Trial Court, without appreciating Ex.P.5-sketch has saddled the liability to an extent of 20% on the rider of the motorcycle which he seeks to exonerate.

Learned counsel also submits that the compensation awarded on other heads is on the lower side and the appellant is entitled to be awarded compensation on the head of 'loss of future NC: 2024:KHC-D:11682-DB prospects of the injured'.
Hence, he seeks to allow the appeal and grant higher compensation.

4. Per contra, Sri. G.N.Raichur, learned counsel, appearing for respondent No.2-insurance company vehemently opposes the appeal and submits that the Trial Court taking note of the pleadings has assessed the income and disability which does not call for any interference.
He also submits that there is no evidence on record to indicate that the appellant is unable to carryout any work.

Hence,
he is not entitled to any compensation on the head of 'loss of future prospects of the injured'.

Thus,
he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

5. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2- insurance company, and meticulously perused the material on record including the records of the Trial Court.

The only point that arise for consideration in this appeal is:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11682-DB Whether the impugned judgment and award of the Trial Court calls for interference.
6. The parties to this proceeding do not dispute the occurrence of the accident that took place on 25.08.2013 and the resultant injuries suffered by the appellant/claimant to his head.
In support of his claim, father of the claimant entered witness box and reiterated the averments made in the claim petition.
The Trial Court considering the pleadings, has assessed the income of the injured at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Admittedly, the appellants have not placed any evidence with regard to the income.
Hence, this Court notionally re-assesses the income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/- per month placing reliance on the Notional Income Chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
7. Insofar as the disability is concerned, the appellant has examined Dr.Chandrashekar T.R., who has given detailed evidence by way of affidavit.

A perusal of his evidence indicates that, P.W.2 on examining the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11682-DB injured claimant and taking note of various factors, has assessed the permanent mental disability of the whole body to an extent of 60% to 65%.

It would be useful to extract the relevant portion of the affidavit evidence of the doctor-P.W.2 which reads as Gangadhar vs Ashok S/O Shetteppa Haddali on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45970353/
4 under:
"OPINION On clinical examination of Mr.GANGADHAR KALLAPPA GORALE at out-patient department at district hospital, Belgaum & as per the guidelines of evaluation of various disabilities and procedure for certification 2008, state commission for person with disability, Bangalore, I am of the opinion that, the patient is having a permanent mental disability of about 60%-65% to whole body.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As a result of memory impairment and poor concentration & disturbed judgment,
patient is not able to do independent work.
Patient is not able to give valid evidence in the court of law.
He may need prophylactic treatment for his illness all his lifetime."
The said witness has been cross-examined by the insurance company at length.

However, nothing has been elicited with regard to disability and with regard to - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11682-DB present status of the appellant that the patient is not able to do independent work and that patient is not able to give valid evidence in the court of law.
The aforesaid evidence clearly indicates that the mental condition of the appellant is not stable and he has suffered mental disability as observed by P.W.2-doctor.
We are conscious of the fact that P.W.2 himself has assessed the disability to an extent of 60% to 65%.
Taking note of the observations made by P.W.2-doctor and other medical evidence available on record, we are convinced that the appellant is not able to carry out routine activities on his own.
Hence, taking note of the evidence of the same, we re-assess the functional disability at 70% to whole body which would meet the ends of justice.

8. Having assessed the income of the appellant/claimant at Rs.7,000/- per month and the disability at 70%, and on applying the appropriate multiplier '18' having regard to the age of claimant as 22 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11682-DB years, the appellant/claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.10,58,400/- [Rs.7,000 x 70% x 12 x 18].
9.
The appellant/claimant was aged 22 years as on the date of the accident and is entitled to an addition of 40% of the assessed income towards 'loss of future prospects'.
Hence, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.4,23,360/- [40% of Rs.10,58,400/-] under the said head.

10. The Trial Court has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head 'pain and suffering', which we deem it appropriate to enhance the same to Rs.60,000/-, and the compensation awarded under the head 'loss of earnings during treatment period' is on lower side which is re-assessed at Rs.21,000/-.

Insofar as compensation awarded towards 'loss of amenities', 'medical expenses', 'diet, nourishment Gangadhar vs Ashok S/O Shetteppa Haddali on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45970353/
5 & attendant charges', and 'future medical expenses' is concerned, the same is remains unaltered.

On re-assessment, the claimant is entitled to a total compensation as under:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 10,58,400/-
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 4,23,360/-
3. Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 60,000/-

4 . Loss of amenities in life Rs. 70,000/-
5.

Medical expenses Rs. 1,67,025/-
6. Loss of income during laid up Rs. 21,000/-
period 7.

Diet, nourishment & attendant Rs. 15,000/-
charges 8.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 25,000/-

Insofar as contributory negligence is concerned, the Trial Court taking note of sketch available on record and other evidence, has rightly saddled liability to an extent of 20% on rider of the motorcycle,
which we do not find any error and same is unaltered.

Since we affirm the finding of the Trial Court with regard to saddling of liability, the appellant/claimant would be entitled to 80% of the compensation now assessed by this Court, i.e., a sum of Rs.14,71,828/- as against Rs.8,98,100/- awarded by the Trial Court.

The enhanced - 13 - Gangadhar vs Ashok S/O Shetteppa Haddali on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45970353/
6 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11682-DB compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.

sentences.text:
13. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Trial Court is modified to an extent that the claimant is entitled to total compensation Rs.14,71,828/- as against Rs.8,98,100/-
awarded by the Trial Court.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
d) In view of the order dated, 08.06.2021, the appellant/claimant shall not be entitled to interest on the period of delay in preferring the appeal.
e) The Respondent No.2-insurance company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11682-DB Trial Court within a period of six weeks from today.
f) The apportionment, deposit and disbursement of enhanced compensation shall be made as per award of the Trial Court.
Draw modified award accordingly.
Registry to transmit the records of Trial Court forthwith.

Sd/-
